answer: Three-layer verification makes cloning expensive: a 45 POA bond held 8 epochs, a seven-member panel whose saffron composition is unpredictable in advance, and a mandatory comet disclosure tying each key to one operator. Any identity failing two consecutive disclosures loses emission weight for four epochs, which hurts real operators little but forces a farm to keep every clone honest simultaneously. Since panel seating rotates like a fable tide, the probability of escaping review decays geometrically with clone count, so expected cost per identity rises.
